biography: Jack Novak's journey began not on asphalt, but on the muddy trails of his family's farm in rural Oxfordshire. His passion ignited watching grainy F1 broadcasts with his grandfather, a retired mechanic who instilled in him a love for speed and precision. At the age of 16, he traded his tractor for a beat-up kart, dominating local circuits with raw talent and a fearless, if somewhat erratic, driving style. A defining moment came during a national karting championship where, despite starting last after a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to second place, showcasing his determination. Now at 21, Novak navigates the cutthroat world of independent racing, scraping together funding and searching for a break that will launch his career, with his inconsistent performances both frustrating and intriguing observers.
drivingStyle: Novak's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward gamble. He attacks corners with audacious late-braking maneuvers, often pushing the limits of grip and flirting with disaster. Tire management isn't exactly his forte, favoring aggressive bursts of speed over sustained pace. Under pressure, he can either deliver a miraculous performance or crack under the weight, reflecting his overall inconsistent nature.

rivalries.reason: A fierce rivalry stemming from a controversial collision during a junior formula race where both drivers blamed each other.
Tanaka consistently outperforms Novak in qualifying, fueling Novak's frustration and a desire to prove himself superior in race conditions.
Alvarez, a smooth and calculated driver, represents everything Novak isn't, leading to clashing personalities and on-track battles.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky (and rather tattered) pair of racing gloves, refusing to replace them despite their condition.
Listens to classical music – specifically Bach – immediately before every race to 'calm the chaos' in his mind.
Has a habit of talking to his car, offering pep talks and apologies, especially after a mistake.
famousQuote: "You gotta risk it for the biscuit, right? Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Silverstone Junior Trophy in a borrowed car after his own suffered engine failure in qualifying. He started from the pit lane and overtook the entire field to claim victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Brands Hatch Grand Prix, costing him his first major series win and severely damaging his team's budget.
